- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp spikes or volatility events.
- Model overestimates prices in the latter half of the 30-day horizon, particularly when true outcomes show a sharp downward correction or mean reversion.
- Model fails to capture sudden, large downward moves (e.g., 34.33 in Example 1, 45.93 in Example 2) — often underestimates magnitude or delays recognition.
- Model exhibits “overshoot” behavior after price spikes — forecasts rise too quickly and then flatten or dip too early, missing the true peak or trough.
- Model shows persistent bias toward higher prices in low-volatility periods, failing to adjust for mean reversion or seasonal patterns.
- Model tends to ignore or misweight recent history — especially when true outcomes deviate sharply from the 30-day average, leading to lagged corrections.
- Model overfits to recent trends, leading to overconfidence in upward momentum, especially when true outcomes show reversal or consolidation.
